desc: Between 10 and 12 February 2023, US fighters shot down three unidentified objects over Alaska, the Yukon and Lake Huron, in the days after the Chinese surveillance balloon was destroyed off South Carolina. A Secret memorandum dated 14 February 2023 from Janice Charette, Clerk of the Privy Council, to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and National Security Advisor Jody Thomas records that 'The full exploitation of UAP #20, which was engaged by the U.S. on February 10, 2023, has not yet been completed,' describing an object roughly the size of a small car at 40,000 feet, 'cylindrical and silver-ish gray' with no apparent propulsion system, which broke apart on sea ice near Prudhoe Bay. The Yukon object, tracked as UAP #23, 'remains unverified' as to 'function, method of propulsion, or affiliation to any nation-state.' The Lake Huron object was destroyed on 12 February 2023 by an AIM-9X fired from one of two F-16CMs of the Minnesota Air National Guard's 148th Fighter Wing at roughly 20,000 feet; a pilot reported 'In the targeting pod, I can't tell if it's metallic or what, but I can see like lines coming down below it.' None of the three were recovered intact. Infrared footage of the Lake Huron engagement was not released until 22 May 2026, through the PURSUE initiative, and the source entry noted an unusual absence of 'substantiated chain-of-custody.' Sean Kirkpatrick's retrospective characterisation - 'We scrambled jets and shot down a bunch of things. Do you know what we shot down? Balloons' - is recorded here as a denial artefact, since the Canadian government's own contemporaneous Secret memo says the objects' function and propulsion were unknown.
